paragraphs.text: Otofaciocervical (OFC) syndrome is clinically similar to branchiootorenal (BOR) syndrome but has features beyond those of BOR syndrome (Rickard et al., 2001). Estefanía et al. (2006) described it as having trophic alterations of the face and shoulder girdle in addition to the malformations seen in BOR syndrome.

paragraphs.text: Dallapiccola and Mingarelli (1995) described a sporadic patient with OFC syndrome. The distinguishing features were a long face with a narrow nose, high arched palate, prominent and dysmorphic ears, long neck, sloping shoulders and clavicles, winged, low, and laterally set scapulae, tetralogy of Fallot, and deafness secondary to cochlear malformation. Preauricular tags, lacrimal duct stenosis, and renal malformations were absent.

paragraphs.text: Dallapiccola and Mingarelli (1995) noted that some features of the original OFC family, including lateral cervical fistulae, had suggested that OFC syndrome might be a variant of BOR syndrome. In their sporadic patient, preauricular tags, lacrimal duct stenosis, and renal malformations were absent, while distinct facial and radiographic findings and markedly downward-sloping shoulders were present. They concluded that this supported OFC syndrome being a unique, clinically recognizable entity. In contrast, Rickard et al. (2001) found a deletion of the EYA1 gene region in a patient with OFC syndrome and concluded that OFC syndrome is allelic with BOR syndrome.

paragraphs.text: Pohl et al. (2013) studied a large consanguineous Turkish family with an autosomal recessive form of otofaciocervical syndrome. They characterized it by facial dysmorphism, external ear anomalies with preauricular pits and hearing impairment, branchial cysts or fistulas, anomalies of the vertebrae and shoulder girdle, and mild intellectual disability. They performed whole-exome sequencing on a pooled DNA sample from 4 affected family members. The only novel homozygous variant they identified was a c.497G-T transversion in the PAX1 gene (167411), predicted to cause a gly166-to-val (G166V) substitution within the highly conserved paired-box domain. The variant cosegregated with the disease in the family. In a dual luciferase reporter assay of an Nkx3-2 promoter regulatory sequence in HEK293T cells, mouse Pax1 carrying the corresponding G157V mutation produced significantly less transactivation than wildtype, indicating that the mutant protein had reduced DNA-binding affinity.

paragraphs.text: Rickard et al. (2001) combined a fluorescent quantitative multiplex PCR dosage assay for EYA1 exons 7, 9, and 13 with microsatellite marker analysis. They identified de novo deletions of the EYA1 gene and the surrounding region in 2 patients whose complex phenotypes included features of BOR syndrome. One of these patients had OFC syndrome and carried a large heterozygous deletion of the EYA1 gene region. The authors concluded that OFC syndrome is allelic with BOR syndrome and is a contiguous gene deletion syndrome involving EYA1.

paragraphs.text: Estefanía et al. (2006) found a single-nucleotide substitution in a splice site of the EYA1 gene in a patient with OFC syndrome. The earlier hypothesis was that OFC syndrome resulted from contiguous deletions of EYA1 and adjacent genes. The authors concluded that OFC syndrome can be caused not only by major rearrangements but also by point mutations that alter the EYA1 reading frame.
